findings.title: Cache status stays stale in the UI after deleting the cache
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component. The connected-calendars query also runs with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. As a result, after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data is unreliable for bumping updatedAt
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it relies on Prisma injecting `@updatedAt` into an `updateMany` whose data is empty, which is fragile. The repository method is also typed with `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which allows relation inputs, but `updateMany` only accepts `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, so the signature is wrong. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly and use the UpdateManyMutationInput type. This also adds an extra write on every cache refresh, and the PR description itself says the frontend does not use this value.

findings.title: Widening UserWithCalendars breaks other callers
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This function is exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` (`getConnectedDestinationCalendars`) and used by other code paths. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select these fields, so any other caller that builds a user with the old select will fail type-checking. Nothing inside this function reads the new fields, so the widening is unnecessary.

findings.title: Plain Error returns 500 instead of a proper tRPC error
findings.body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`. tRPC surfaces this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), which logs a server error and gives clients the wrong status. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `FORBIDDEN` instead.

findings.title: Cache status counts expired cache entries
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all `CalendarCache` rows without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. A credential whose only cache rows have expired, and are therefore never served, is still shown as having a cache with a last-updated time. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause.

findings.title: Existing rows get the migration time as updatedAt, and the header comment is wrong
findings.body: Every pre-existing cache row gets `updatedAt = NOW()` at migration time. The UI will therefore show a misleading "Last updated" time for legacy caches until they are refreshed. Separately, the auto-generated warning says the column is added "without a default value", which contradicts the actual `DEFAULT NOW()` statement below it.

findings.title: Timestamp is always formatted in en-US
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `"en-US"` locale, so non-English users see US date formatting inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale from `useLocale` (`i18n.language`) instead.

findings.title: macOS-only `sed -i ''` and cwd-relative env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` only works with BSD sed. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty `''` is parsed as the script, so the command fails and the .env file is not updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current working directory rather than the script's location, so running the script from elsewhere edits or creates the wrong file. `cleanup` also exits with status 0 on failure paths.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on tsx, which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: `npx tsx` is not in the package's dependencies, so npx downloads an unpinned version at runtime. This breaks offline or locked-down setups and makes runs non-reproducible. Add `tsx` as a devDependency.
